summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and a history of gastrointestinal bleeding was admitted for worsening right hip pain over three weeks, without fever or trauma. Initial concern included septic arthritis or avascular necrosis, but imaging showed no fracture or necrosis, and hip aspiration revealed clear fluid with no organisms or white blood cells. Cultures were negative, ruling out infection. Pain was attributed to degenerative joint changes and possibly renal osteodystrophy. He was managed with acetaminophen and oxycodone, and evaluated for GI bleeding risk with a MRE that showed a non-bleeding jejunal polyp. Digoxin was held due to elevated levels. He was discharged to a rehab facility for a short-term course of physical therapy and continued dialysis, with stable pain and no complications during admission.
problems: Pain in joint, pelvic region and thigh
